Theme gallery for sign-off · 23 November 2026

68 new themes for Radiant

Radiant has seven built-in themes today. This page proposes 68 more in eight families. Some are new palettes and typefaces. Many change what a mind map is drawn as: a subway map, a circuit board, a constellation, gold-mended ceramic. Every picture is drawn from a real theme spec, so what you approve is what gets built.

68proposed themes, 24 dark and 44 light
5ready now with the current engine
29need finish work already proposed in the visual review
34need new drawing code
  1. Compare. Every sample is the same 16-node map, so differences are the theme and nothing else.
  2. Switch the preview. Full design is the intent. Today's engine is what you would get if the theme were added to the current code with no other work.
  3. Decide. Approve, Maybe or Drop on each card, with an optional note. Choices are saved in this browser.
  4. Send it back. Copy decisions puts a plain-text summary on your clipboard. Paste it to me and I will build the approved set.

What ships today 7 themes

For reference, the current built-ins redrawn with the same sample map and the current engine's rules. Colours and settings are read from core/model/themes.ts.

What it takes to build them

EffortThemesMeaning
Ready now5Uses colours, typeface, shapes and branch styles the app already has.
Needs finish work29Needs items already proposed in the visual review: surfaces, tinting, shadows, glow or textured strokes.
Needs new drawing code34Needs something the renderer cannot draw yet: new routing, layered strokes, markers, or new node and centre shapes.

Every theme falls back cleanly. A theme that needs new drawing code can ship first with its palette, typeface and nearest existing branch style, which is what Today's engine shows, and gain its full look when the renderer catches up.

Full design also assumes two craft fixes from the visual review on every theme: branches fanning out along the centre shape, and round line ends. Today's engine shows them without.

All typefaces ship with macOS, so nothing has to be licensed or bundled. The theme format already accepts any font family. Only the picker in the theme editor is limited to five.

CapabilityThemes using itWhere it comes from
Canvas surface47Review item B5
Shadows20Review item B2
New centre shape19New: one drawing routine per shape
Tip tint or depth colour18Review item B3
Layered stroke16New: the same path drawn several times
Node markers15New: a glyph drawn at a node or tip
Glow12New: a blur pass or a wide soft stroke
Tip dots11Review item A3
Single limb colour10Small: branch colour separate from marker colour
Textured stroke9Review item B6
New node shape9New: one drawing routine per shape
Labels in branch colour6Small: a theme flag in the style resolver
New routing5New: a path builder per route
Ink blending2New: multiply blending between strokes

How these were made

Research. I looked at how large other products' theme sets are and what they vary. Xmind's blog describes 32 colour themes with six variations each. MindNode has a theme gallery with names such as Elegant, Fresh, Modern and Roadmap, plus personal themes. SimpleMind lists more than 15 style sheets. In those sources the variation is colour, shape and line style. None of them changes what the map is drawn as.

Invention. About half of this set goes past that. The Worlds family and several others keep the same tree and change the drawing rules: 45-degree transit lines with stations, copper traces with solder pads, stars joined by faint lines, cracks filled with gold, roads with signs, red string between pinned notes. Those ideas are mine and are not taken from another product.

Palettes with a source. Nightfall uses the Nord palette and Pastel Night uses Catppuccin Mocha; both were confirmed by search. Velvet uses Dracula's colours from memory, which the search did not confirm. Colour Safe is based on the Okabe-Ito set. All four are open palettes, but check their licences before shipping themes that name them.

The samples. Each picture is an SVG generated from the theme's spec: palette, typeface, branch route and stroke, node shape, centre shape, canvas surface and effects. Text is measured in a real browser so labels and lines meet. Today's engine redraws the same spec using only the app's five branch styles, its box, underline and none shapes, a flat canvas and its segment formula.

Contrast. Label contrast is computed against the canvas colour and every theme reaches the project's 4.5:1 gate. Faintest branch is the lowest contrast of any branch colour against the canvas. It is shown in amber below 3:1. Soft themes such as Sorbet, Clay and Spotlight are below that on purpose, and so is one colour in the current Clean theme.

Not done. I did not use the Codex CLI to paint the samples. A painted image would look richer but could not be reproduced by the renderer, so it would not be a reliable thing to sign off. Nothing in the app was changed, and these themes are not yet in the code.
